newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs, pork belly futures end mostly higher.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs, pork belly futures end mostly higher.

text.p: CME hog futures finished mostly higher on scattered short covering while pork belly futures rallied to the day's highs at the close on local short covering and buy stops, traders said.
Hog futures finished 0.175 cent per lb higher to 0.300 lower with only April off and February unchanged at 75.450 cents. Pork bellies ended 0.675 to 0.150 cent higher led by February at 78.050.

Bitter cold weather pushing through the Midwest and expected continued light hog marketings supported December hog futures after early resistance linked to lower pork cutout values and scattered long liquidation, traders said.

Back months showed little direction as market watchers started to look to the holidays and upcoming government reports, sources said. The monthly USDA Cold Storage Report will be released by the USDA on Friday and the quarterly Hogs and Pigs report numbers will be released December 27.

Early estimates on the upcoming Hogs and Pigs report point to all hogs on farms at 95 to 100 percent of a year ago with numbers kept for breeding at 100 to 103 percent and hogs kept for market at 94 to 99 percent of last year.

The upcoming storage report will likely have some effect on nearby pork belly futures which rallied late Wednesday. Ideas of low stocks added to local short covering linked to holding of technical support and recent light hog slaughter. Closing buy stops pushed prices up to days high at the closing bell, traders said.

Tuesday's CME out-of-town report provided early underlying support but estimates for Friday's storage data were potentially more bullish. Traders noted that analysts' estimates pointed to total U.S. belly stocks as of December 1 under year-ago and historical levels.
Estimates on the report ranged from 26.6 million to 32.2 million lbs and averaged 29 million lbs, compared with 37.092 million on hand last year and a 10-year average on hand of 45.5 million lbs.
In hog options, commission houses bought February 78 and 80 calls and October 60 and 62 calls. In belly options, commission houses were actively on both sides of February 78 calls, pit sources said.
